title: Registration data can be linked to an existing identity
description: The authentication service receives a strong identifier set during parent registration, including email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code. These attributes can be correlated with existing records or external datasets, allowing the newly created account and future activity to be linked to the same individual across contexts.
assumptions: The service stores or can access prior records keyed by email, government ID, or similar identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether linkage is modeled via stored identifiers or cross-context correlation.

title: Direct identification of the parent during registration
description: The registration flow includes directly identifying data such as name, email, and government ID. Anyone with access to the transmitted or processed data can identify the parent without needing auxiliary information.
assumptions: The authentication service or intermediaries can view plaintext values at some stage of processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability through direct identifiers.

title: Disclosure of sensitive registration attributes in transit or at intake
description: The flow carries sensitive personal data and credentials, including password and government ID. If transport protection, endpoint handling, logging controls, or input-processing safeguards are weak, these values may be exposed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Threat includes exposure through network interception, reverse proxies, application logs, monitoring tools, or debugging traces.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure on a data flow; exact subtree may differ by whether disclosure is in transit, in logs, or at the receiving process.

title: Excessive collection discloses more personal data than necessary for authentication
description: Collecting government ID and full name as part of basic account registration may exceed what is necessary for authentication alone. Requesting and processing unnecessary attributes increases privacy exposure because more personal data is revealed to the service than needed for the stated purpose.
assumptions: The primary purpose of this flow is account creation/authentication rather than regulated identity proofing that strictly requires government ID.
uncertainty_note: This is mapped as disclosure/exposure through over-collection; exact node id may differ because some LINDDUN Pro catalogs place data minimization issues under disclosure or non-compliance-related branches.

title: Parent may be unable to prove what registration details or consent were submitted
description: If the authentication service does not provide verifiable receipts or tamper-evident records for the registration submission, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate what data was provided, whether a six-digit code was entered, or what terms were accepted at registration time.
assumptions: The system may not issue signed confirmations or preserve auditable evidence visible to the user.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of evidence/repudiation in a registration flow.

title: Insufficient transparency about why government ID and code are required
description: The parent may not understand the purpose of collecting government ID, name, email, password, and the six-digit code, how long they will be retained, or whether they are used for identity proofing, fraud prevention, or account recovery. This undermines user awareness and informed expectations.
assumptions: The interface does not clearly explain purposes, retention, recipients, and optional versus mandatory fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact subtree may vary.

title: Registration may violate data minimization or lawful-basis requirements
description: If the service collects government ID or other registration attributes without necessity, proportionality, clear purpose limitation, or an appropriate legal basis, the flow may be non-compliant with privacy obligations. The risk is heightened because the flow includes both credentials and official identity data.
assumptions: Applicable privacy law or policy imposes minimization, purpose limitation, notice, and lawful-basis obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance; exact node depends on the governing obligation being assessed.

title: Stored parent account record may reveal identity
description: Storing a parent account in the users collection can directly identify a natural person through account attributes such as name, email address, phone number, username, or persistent account identifiers.
assumptions: The parent account record contains direct identifiers or unique account identifiers tied to an individual.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identity disclosure may vary.

title: Parent account records may be linkable across services or contexts
description: If the stored parent account includes stable identifiers, device identifiers, email addresses, or reused internal IDs, records in the users collection may be linked with other datasets or transactions, enabling profiling of the parent across contexts.
assumptions: Identifiers in the stored account are stable over time or reused in other systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability may differ.

title: Sensitive parent attributes may be disclosed from the users collection
description: The stored parent account may contain personal or sensitive attributes such as contact details, child relationship information, authentication metadata, or recovery data. Unauthorized access to the collection could disclose these data.
assumptions: The parent account schema includes personal data beyond a minimal opaque identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure subtree may vary.

title: Storage may exceed data minimization or retention expectations
description: Persisting the full parent account in MongoDB may involve collecting or retaining more personal data than necessary for authentication, or keeping it longer than needed, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: The implementation stores full account objects or retains records without strict minimization/retention controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for detectability/non-compliance-adjacent data disclosure excess; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Stored parent account may violate consent, purpose limitation, or retention obligations
description: If the parent account is stored without a clear lawful basis, without transparent notice, beyond the stated purpose, or without honoring deletion/retention requirements, the flow can create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require purpose limitation, transparency, retention limits, or user rights handling for account data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact non-compliance subtree may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of user data in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the returned user data includes more attributes than necessary for the parent-facing use case, the flow reveals personal information beyond data minimization needs.
assumptions: Assumes the response may include profile or account attributes in addition to the token, and not all are strictly necessary for the parent at this step.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for attribute disclosure / unnecessary personal data exposure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability via stable identifiers in JWT or payload
description: If the JWT or accompanying user data contains stable identifiers such as account ID, subject claim, email address, or device-correlatable values, the parent user's actions across sessions or services may become linkable.
assumptions: Assumes the token or payload contains persistent identifiers and may be reused across relying components or over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability caused by persistent identifiers in protocol messages.

title: Identifiability of the authenticated child/user to the parent beyond necessity
description: The combination of JWT claims and user data may directly identify the underlying user or child account to the parent, even where only authorization status or limited relationship information is needed.
assumptions: Assumes the parent does not need full identifying details for every authentication event.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identifiability through exposed identity attributes.

title: Non-compliant sharing of personal data in auth response
description: Returning JWT claims and user data to the parent may violate purpose limitation, data minimization, or transparency obligations if the data shared exceeds what was consented to or documented for this authentication purpose.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements constrain what child/user data may be disclosed to a parent during authentication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/legal non-compliance; exact node mapping may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent can plausibly deny receipt or use of authentication data
description: If receipt of the JWT and user data is not adequately logged or bound to the parent session, the parent user may later deny having received or acted upon the authentication response, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Assumes weak audit logging or lack of proof of delivery/receipt for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation/accountability gaps on message receipt.

title: Insufficient transparency about JWT contents and user-data use
description: The parent user may not understand what personal data is embedded in the JWT or returned alongside it, how long it remains valid, or how it will be used by downstream components, reducing user awareness and informed control.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain token contents, retention, recipients, or purposes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node label may vary.

title: Authentication service can identify the child via parent email used as login credential
description: The login flow transmits a parent email address together with a password to the authentication service. Even if the account is intended for a child user, the parent email is a direct identifier that allows the service to identify and single out the household or parent-linked account during authentication.
assumptions: The parent email is stored or processed as the account identifier during login.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for direct identification through credentials, but exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Repeated logins using the same parent email enable linkability of child sessions
description: Using the same parent email as the username across login attempts allows the authentication service to link multiple sessions and events to the same account or household over time, potentially building a profile of the child user's activity patterns.
assumptions: The service logs authentication attempts or associates sessions with the supplied email/account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent account identifier; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Login credentials disclose personal data to the authentication service
description: The flow reveals personal data during authentication, including the parent email address and the fact that a child is attempting to access the service through that account. This may disclose household relationships and account existence to the authentication service beyond what the child may expect.
assumptions: The authentication service can observe and retain the submitted email and associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for exposure of credentials and relationship information; exact node id may differ.

title: Authentication attempts may disclose account existence through differential handling
description: If the authentication service responds differently for valid versus invalid parent email addresses, the login flow can disclose whether a parent email is registered. This leaks personal information about account ownership and potentially the child's enrollment status.
assumptions: The service exposes distinguishable errors, timing, or workflow differences for unknown versus known emails.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure via account enumeration behavior.

title: Use of parent email for child login may exceed data minimization expectations
description: Authenticating a child user with a parent email may process more identifying personal data than necessary for the child to log in. If a less identifying child-specific or pseudonymous credential could be used, this flow may conflict with data minimization or child-privacy compliance expectations.
assumptions: Alternative, less identifying authentication designs are feasible and applicable in the deployment context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for excessive collection/use of identifying data; exact numbering may vary.

title: Child may be unaware that parent identity is used and processed during login
description: The child login flow uses the parent's email address as a credential, which may not be transparent to the child or parent in terms of how identity and relationship data are processed, logged, or reused. This can undermine user awareness about privacy implications of authentication.
assumptions: The interface or notices do not clearly explain why parent email is required and how it is used.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Exposure of child status and profile data to unintended recipients on the client side
description: The flow delivers a JWT explicitly indicating userType=child together with child profiles to the Child User endpoint. If the token or profile payload is exposed through insecure client storage, browser history, shared devices, screen observation, or interception after delivery, sensitive information about a minor and associated profile details may be disclosed to unintended parties.
assumptions: Assumes the child uses a device or client environment where other parties may access displayed or stored data, or that transport/session protections may be insufficient in some deployments.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; without the exact LINDDUN Pro tree variant, I.1 is used generically for information disclosure/exposure.

title: JWT enables linkability of the child's activities across sessions or services
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers, persistent subject claims, or other unique attributes, the child can be linked across multiple sessions, devices, or relying components. Combining the token with child profile data can further strengthen correlation of the same minor over time.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT includes stable identifiers or claims reused across requests or contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort generic mapping for linkability; exact subtree may differ depending on the LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: JWT claims reveal more personal data than necessary
description: The JWT and returned child profiles may include excessive claims or attributes beyond what the child-facing client strictly needs. Over-disclosure increases privacy risk by exposing age-related status, identifiers, preferences, or account metadata unnecessarily.
assumptions: Assumes the token/profile schema may contain optional or convenience fields not required for the immediate interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; used here for unnecessary attribute disclosure/data minimization concerns.

title: Identifiability of a minor through token and profile attributes
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, the combination of JWT claims and child profile attributes may uniquely identify the child within the system or to someone with auxiliary knowledge. This is especially sensitive because the data subject is a child.
assumptions: Assumes profile fields or token claims include quasi-identifiers or unique account references.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic node id for identifiability; exact node may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: Insufficient transparency or lawful basis indicators for delivering child profile data
description: The flow returns child profiles and a child-designating JWT, but the child may not be adequately informed what profile data is included, why it is needed, how long it will be retained, or with whom it will be shared. For child data, missing or unclear privacy notices and consent/authorization handling can create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly communicate privacy information at the point of authentication/profile delivery or lacks age-appropriate notice/authorization mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapped generically to non-compliance/transparency-related concerns.

title: Child may be unaware of privacy implications of the received JWT and profile data
description: A child user may not understand that the authentication token and profile payload can be reused, stored, or exposed by the client application. This can undermine informed control over personal data and increase the chance of accidental sharing or misuse.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or client does not present age-appropriate explanations of token use and profile visibility.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic node id for unawareness; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Collection of directly identifying child attributes
description: The flow sends highly identifying personal data for a child profile—name, date of birth, gender, and government ID—to Child Profile Management. This enables direct identification of the child and creates privacy risk if the data is not strictly necessary or is exposed.
assumptions: Assumes the child profile can be tied to a real-world child identity and that government ID is a strong identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identifying data collection may differ.

title: Linkability of child profile to parent and other records
description: The combination of child name, DOB, gender, and government ID can link this child profile to other internal or external records, and to the parent user's account, enabling correlation across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the system stores the child profile alongside parent account data or can correlate via identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong even if exact subtree label differs.

title: Detectability of child enrollment or existence of a child profile
description: Transmission of child-identifying data to the profile-management process may allow an observer or internal party to detect that a child profile is being created or exists, revealing sensitive family-status information.
assumptions: Assumes metadata, logs, or traffic visibility could reveal the occurrence of this flow even without full content access.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability subtree node may differ; this is a best-fit mapping.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child personal data in transit or processing
description: The flow contains sensitive personal data about a child, including government ID. If intercepted, logged insecurely, or exposed within processing, unauthorized parties could learn the child's identity and attributes.
assumptions: Assumes there is some risk of interception, excessive logging, or overbroad internal access during receipt and handling by P3.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific to data in transit or processing.

title: Unawareness about extent and purpose of child data collection
description: The parent may not fully understand why each child attribute is required, how long it will be retained, who can access it, or whether government ID is mandatory, leading to uninformed submission of the child's data.
assumptions: Assumes notice/consent and just-in-time explanations may be insufficient or absent at profile creation time.
uncertainty_note: Exact unawareness subtree node is approximate.

title: Non-compliant collection of child data beyond necessity or lawful basis
description: Collecting a child's name, DOB, gender, and especially government ID at profile creation may exceed data minimization requirements or require specific lawful basis, parental authorization handling, retention limits, and child-data safeguards. If these are not met, the flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy laws or platform policies impose heightened requirements for children's data and government identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subtree node is approximate because no jurisdiction or policy baseline was provided.

title: Insufficient evidence of parent submission or authorization
description: If the system does not capture adequate proof that the parent user submitted and authorized the child profile details, either party may later dispute what data was provided or whether the submission was authorized.
assumptions: Assumes profile creation may have legal or operational significance and audit evidence may be limited.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related node id is a best-fit estimate from memory.

title: Unauthorized modification of child profile data before storage
description: The child profile management process may update or overwrite profile attributes without proper authorization checks or integrity protection, causing inaccurate or maliciously altered child data to be stored in the childprofiles collection.
assumptions: P3 accepts profile update requests from upstream actors or services and writes directly to DS2.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro integrity subtree labeling may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile contents from stored records
description: The childprofiles collection stores sensitive child profile attributes. If access controls, query restrictions, or encryption are insufficient, stored profiles may be disclosed to unauthorized parties, exposing personal data about children.
assumptions: DS2 contains personally identifiable or sensitive child-related attributes and may be accessible by multiple components or administrators.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; disclosure subtree numbering may vary across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Linkability of child records across updates and contexts
description: Repeated store/update operations to the same child profile can rely on stable identifiers or consistent attribute combinations, enabling records in the childprofiles collection to be linked across sessions, services, or contexts and building a more complete profile of the child.
assumptions: Profiles use persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers that remain stable over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact linkability subtree node may differ.

title: Loss of integrity of stored child profiles in MongoDB
description: Stored child profiles may be corrupted, partially updated, or tampered with in the database, resulting in inaccurate profile data being used later for decisions or display.
assumptions: Database writes may not be atomic for all profile fields, or privileged actors/services can modify records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact integrity subtree labeling may differ.

title: Retention or secondary use of child profile data beyond stated purpose
description: Child profile data stored in the collection may be retained longer than necessary or reused for purposes beyond child profile management without appropriate consent, legal basis, or policy enforcement, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The system processes regulated children's personal data and retention/purpose-limitation controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; non-compliance subtree numbering may vary.

title: Identifiability of a child from stored profile attributes
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, combinations of profile fields in the childprofiles collection may uniquely identify a child, especially when combined with other available datasets or metadata.
assumptions: Profiles contain direct identifiers or sufficiently distinctive quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact unlinkability/identifiability subtree numbering may differ.

title: Search and interaction activity can be linked to the same child across sessions
description: Search queries, video requests, likes, and comments sent by the child user may carry stable identifiers, account context, device fingerprints, or network metadata that allow the service to link multiple actions to the same child over time, building a persistent activity profile.
assumptions: The service receives or can derive persistent identifiers or metadata alongside the flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers across interactions.

title: Video interactions may identify the child user
description: The combination of account identifiers, IP address, device data, and distinctive search/request/like/comment patterns may allow the Video Management Service to identify the child user directly or single them out from other users.
assumptions: The service can access account, device, or network-level metadata associated with the flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from direct or indirect identifiers; exact subtree may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Searches, likes, and comments disclose the child's interests and preferences
description: The content of search terms, requested videos, likes, and comments can reveal personal interests, habits, emotional state, social relationships, or potentially sensitive topics about the child, exposing more information than necessary for basic service delivery.
assumptions: The service stores or analyzes the semantic content of the child's interactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from message content; exact node naming may differ.

title: Interaction history enables profiling and inference about the child
description: Aggregating the child's searches, viewing requests, likes, and comments over time enables the service to infer preferences, routines, maturity level, vulnerabilities, or other derived attributes, potentially supporting recommendation manipulation or targeted treatment.
assumptions: The service retains interaction history and performs analytics or profiling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/inference from observable behavior history; exact node may differ by catalog version.

title: Child may be unaware of collection and secondary use of interaction data
description: The child user may not understand that searches, requests, likes, and comments are collected, retained, analyzed for recommendations, moderation, safety monitoring, or other secondary purposes beyond fulfilling the immediate request.
assumptions: Notices are limited, complex, or not age-appropriate for children.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: Processing of child's interaction data may exceed consent or child-privacy requirements
description: Collecting and using a child's search, request, like, and comment data for profiling, personalization, retention, or sharing may violate consent expectations, purpose limitation, data minimization, or child-specific legal obligations if not properly justified and authorized.
assumptions: The user is a child and the service may rely on consent or other legal bases that impose special conditions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with consent/purpose-limitation obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: Child may be unable to deny or contest submitted likes/comments
description: If the service records likes or comments without strong integrity, attribution context, or user-verifiable audit evidence, the child may later be unable to repudiate actions they did not intend, or conversely may be unfairly bound to actions they dispute.
assumptions: The system relies on stored interaction logs as evidence of user actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation/privacy tension around action attribution; exact node may vary.

title: Excessive video metadata stored enables identification of creators or viewers
description: When the Video Management Service stores video metadata in MongoDB, fields such as uploader identifiers, account references, IP-derived location, device details, timestamps, or access history can directly or indirectly identify individuals.
assumptions: The metadata schema may include user/account-linked attributes beyond what is strictly necessary to manage videos.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for identifiability via direct/indirect identifiers in stored data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability across videos and user activities through persistent identifiers
description: A single MongoDB collection holding video metadata can allow records to be linked via stable uploader IDs, channel IDs, tenant IDs, device IDs, tags, or repeated access patterns, enabling correlation of multiple videos and related user actions.
assumptions: Records in DS3 share common identifiers or quasi-identifiers across uploads, edits, retrievals, or analytics-related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability through common identifiers across records; exact subtree may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive video metadata or file references from the datastore
description: If MongoDB records contain titles, descriptions, thumbnails, storage URIs, moderation notes, visibility settings, or embedded file references, unauthorized access to DS3 can disclose personal or sensitive information about data subjects and their content.
assumptions: DS3 stores metadata and possibly references sufficient to locate or retrieve associated video files.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-fit for information disclosure from stored data.

title: Insufficient deletion or retention control for video metadata and associated file references
description: The store/retrieve flow may preserve metadata, soft-deleted records, version history, or pointers to video files longer than expected, preventing effective erasure and extending exposure of personal data.
assumptions: Deletion requests may not fully propagate to all metadata fields, indexes, backups, or linked file references.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data not being deleted or retained too long; exact node label may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that rich metadata and file references are stored and reused
description: Data subjects may not understand that uploading or interacting with videos causes persistent storage of metadata such as timestamps, technical attributes, moderation state, and retrieval-related information in the backend datastore.
assumptions: System notices or UI explanations do not fully describe backend storage practices for video metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency regarding data processing.

title: Storage of video metadata may exceed consent, purpose limitation, or minimization expectations
description: The service may store more metadata than necessary, reuse it for secondary purposes, or retain it beyond the consented or expected purpose, creating non-compliance risks around lawful basis, minimization, and retention.
assumptions: There are policy or regulatory constraints on what metadata may be stored and for how long.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with consent/purpose/retention obligations; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Lack of reliable evidence about metadata creation, modification, or deletion actions
description: If writes and updates from the Video Management Service to MongoDB are not logged with sufficient integrity and attribution, users or operators may later be unable to prove who stored, changed, retrieved, or deleted video-related personal data.
assumptions: Audit logging for datastore operations may be incomplete, mutable, or not attributable to specific actors.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation due to insufficient logging/non-repudiation controls.

title: Storage of child search/watch history reveals sensitive interests and behavior
description: The process stores detailed child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection. Such records can expose sensitive preferences, habits, inferred age-related traits, health, religion, or other intimate aspects of a child if accessed beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: The stored history is granular and tied to an identifiable child profile rather than being fully aggregated or anonymized.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure of stored personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Persistent history enables linkage of child activities over time
description: A centralized datastore of search and watch history tied to a child profile allows multiple events and sessions to be linked together, creating a longitudinal behavioral record for the same child.
assumptions: Records in the collection share a stable child/profile identifier or equivalent correlator.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers/history; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Stored history makes the child profile identifiable
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, detailed search and watch history can single out or re-identify a child profile when combined with account data, device data, timestamps, or unique viewing patterns.
assumptions: The datastore contents can be combined with other available attributes or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from stored data; exact node id may vary.

title: Excessive retention or over-collection of child activity history
description: Storing full search and watch history may exceed what is necessary for the stated service purpose, especially for children, increasing privacy risk through unnecessary accumulation and retention of behavioral data.
assumptions: The system stores raw or long-lived history rather than minimizing, truncating, or expiring it quickly.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/retention concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Secondary use of child history may be insufficiently transparent
description: Users or guardians may not understand that detailed child search and watch history is being stored and potentially used for personalization, recommendations, analytics, or moderation, undermining predictability and awareness.
assumptions: Notice is incomplete, hard to understand, or does not clearly explain storage and downstream uses of child activity history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: Storing child behavioral history may violate child-privacy obligations
description: Persisting child search and watch history can trigger heightened legal and policy obligations around lawful basis, parental consent, purpose limitation, retention limits, and special protections for children's data. If these are not met, the flow creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The service is subject to child privacy requirements and the stored history qualifies as personal data about a child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with privacy/legal obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: Parent identity exposed through authenticated video submission
description: Uploading a video for approval/rejection may require the parent to authenticate or otherwise attach account identifiers, allowing the service to identify the submitting parent and associate the submission with a specific individual.
assumptions: The upload flow carries an account identifier, session token, email, or other parent-linked metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identification is modeled via direct identifiers or account linkage.

title: Uploaded video can be linked to the parent's existing profile or prior submissions
description: The Video Management Service can link the uploaded video and its approval/rejection outcome with the parent's account history, child records, device metadata, or previous uploads, enabling correlation across interactions.
assumptions: The service stores uploads together with persistent account, child, or device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/history.

title: Video content and metadata may disclose personal or sensitive information
description: The uploaded video may reveal the child's image, voice, home environment, school uniforms, routines, or other sensitive details. Associated metadata such as timestamps, filenames, captions, and device information can further disclose personal information.
assumptions: The service receives raw media and may preserve embedded or accompanying metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; disclosure may map to a more specific content- or metadata-disclosure subtree in a full catalog.

title: Approval or rejection outcome reveals information about the parent or child
description: The decision on whether a video is approved or rejected can itself disclose information, such as policy violations, child-related attributes, or inferred behavior, especially if the outcome is visible to internal staff or other systems beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Decision results are stored, logged, or shared with other components or personnel.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is disclosure through derived decision data rather than raw content alone.

title: Parent may be unaware of review, retention, or secondary use of uploaded videos
description: If the service does not clearly communicate how uploaded videos are reviewed, how long they are retained, who can access them, and whether they are reused for moderation improvement or analytics, the parent may be insufficiently informed about processing.
assumptions: Transparency notices are incomplete or not presented in context of upload.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Upload and moderation processing may exceed consent or legal basis
description: Processing the video for approval/rejection may involve collecting more personal data than necessary, retaining it too long, or using it for additional purposes such as training, analytics, or manual review without an appropriate legal basis or valid consent/authorization.
assumptions: The service may perform secondary processing beyond the immediate approval workflow.

title: Parent can plausibly deny having submitted a specific video if submission evidence is weak
